title: Cap set problem
statement: A subset of F_3^n with no three-term arithmetic progression has at most 2.756^n elements.
how_it_was_proved: Ellenberg and Gijswijt, after Croot, Lev and Pach, bound the rank of the tensor 1[x+y+z=0] restricted to the set by counting monomials of low degree: the slice rank of a diagonal tensor equals the size of its support.

sources.cite: J. S. Ellenberg and D. Gijswijt, On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression, Ann. of Math. 185 (2017) 339-343
S. R. Dahmen, J. Hölzl and R. Y. Lewis, Formalizing the solution to the cap set problem, ITP 2019, LIPIcs 141, 15

steps.statement: A polynomial vanishing off a set has a low-degree part controlled by the set
Monomials of degree at most 2n/3 in n variables of degree at most 2 number at most 2.756^n
steps.how: a finite computation of a multinomial sum

steps.statement: Every cap set in F_3^n has at most 3 times that number of points
